faqs.question: What does Fibroblast Growth Factor 23, Plasma measure?
faqs.answer: The test measures the Fibroblast Growth Factor 23 levels in the blood plasma.

faqs.question: Why is Fibroblast Growth Factor 23, Plasma Test Done?
faqs.answer: • FG23 test is done to monitor the progression of chronic kidney disease by monitoring the renal clearance status. • The test aids the diagnosis of hereditary hypophosphatemic rickets and diagnosis and follow-up of tumor-induced osteomalacia.

faqs.question: Who Should Get Fibroblast Growth Factor 23, Plasma Test Done?
faqs.answer: • CKD patients at risk for altered phosphorus metabolism due to malfunctioning of the kidneys. • Patients with bone disorders like hereditary rickets which may affect the phosphorus and vitamin D metabolism. • The test may also be advised for patients with certain types of bone tumors.

faqs.question: What to expect during Fibroblast Growth Factor 23, Plasma test?
faqs.answer: The test requires a blood plasma sample. A tourniquet (elastic) band is placed tightly on the upper arm. The patient is then asked to make a fist. This helps in the build-up of blood filling the veins. The skin is disinfected before needle insertion and the blood sample is collected in vacutainer.

faqs.question: Are any preparations required for Fibroblast Growth Factor 23, Plasma test?
What if results are High/ Low?
faqs.answer: Elevated levels are associated with increased adverse outcome and is a predictor of mortality in CKD. Increased levels are seen in Autosomal Dominant Hypophosphatemic Rickets, X-linked Hypophosphatemia Rickets, Fibrous Dysplasia and tumor induced osteomalacia.
